utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the witness could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Please be seated. Good morning, Ms. Gustafson. Do we need any warning to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There was none in the previous case and I see no reason to have one here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 90327 on the screen not to be broadcast publicly, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sir, do you see on the screen in front of you a witness statement of yours that was read to you in your language a few days ago --

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: -- and that you signed on the 27th of March, 2012?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And is your name and are your other personal details correct on that statement? And please don't mention any of those details publicly.

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And is this statement true and -- to the best of your knowledge and does it accurately reflect the things that you said that are contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if I asked you in court today the questions you were asked when you gave the information in this statement, would you give the Court the same answers that are contained in your statement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this statement under seal, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this statement was read to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, this will be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P4837, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to read a brief summary of the statement and because of the witness's protective measures it will be quite brief and general and in nature. And in that regard I'd like to mention that information about the specific job and tasks that the witness carried out at the time should be discussed in private session because they might reveal his identity. Witness KDZ610 lived in Zvornik in 1992. He describes the outbreak of the conflict in Zvornik on 8 April 1992. The Serbs and the JNA attacked the Muslims of Zvornik and Muslims fled the municipality. KDZ610 provides evidence about the detention of Muslim civilians in Zvornik, including at the Alhos factory, Ekonomija farm and Celopek Dom Kulture. He also provides evidence about mass killings of Muslims in Zvornik municipality, including killings at Drinjaca school and Gero's slaughter-house. That concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sir, I just have one question for you today and it's just a minor point of clarification. In your statement at a couple of places you make reference to the Standard building as the building where the army staff was located, and I'd like to ask you if this is the same building as what's known as the Standard footwear factory or the Novi Standard footwear factory or whether those are different buildings?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: The Standard building was where the army was located, the army and the police. That was a new building. That was the new building of the Standard Zvornik footwear factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we deal with the associated exhibits, Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Those are the exhibits that were listed in the revised 92 ter notification of the 27th of March and they can all be tendered publicly save for 65 ter 23676, which is a map drawn by the witness and it contains his signature, that one should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you do not object to the addition of the documents to the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And as regards the excerpt of video you are only tendering that part of the excerpt?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Except for ones that have already been admitted, they will be all admitted into evidence and be given number in due course. Sir, your evidence was admitted in writing in form -- in the form of your statement in lieu of your oral testimony, as you noted. You'll be further asked by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Further, that you're testifying today with the benefit of pseudonym, image and voice distortion, so whenever you feel like your answer may reveal your real name or identity, then don't hesitate to ask us to go into private session where the people outside this courtroom cannot follow the proceedings at all. Do you also understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to remind myself of this as well, but I kindly ask you to pause between the questions and answers because otherwise the interpreters will not be able to interpret everything that is said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly move into private session, please, because the witness could be identified on the basis of this question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do remember to pause. If you can follow the transcript, when the letter A appears, then it is your turn to speak. Did you have any hostile feelings towards Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you see this A, then it's your turn to speak. Thank you. Did you ever have the wish or intention to have the Muslims exterminated, killed, or expelled?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Although you are not interested in politics, you did notice that there was a political life going on in your municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that after the first democratic multi-party elections for a while there was harmony and do we agree that tensions started when the Party of Democratic Action moved to secede from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Well, what I'd say to that is I'm no politician. I don't know what the intention of the Party of Democratic Action was, whether they wanted to secede or not. Bogic, Bogicevic was up there, the Presidency, what they did -- well, in my view they all wanted to separate from Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I'm not going to dwell on this topic any longer. Do you remember when I and Adil Zulfikarpasic in the summer of 1991 held a public rally aimed at the reconciliation of Serbs and Muslims? Did you attend perhaps?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I was not interested in politics and I did not attend that rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. Then we're going to move on to things that you observed yourself. Is it correct that you observed that there was tension, that there was some organisation going on within the ethnic communities and arming? You do speak about that in your statement, don't you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I observed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any insight, specific insight, or less specific insight into the fact that the Muslim side had the Green Berets, the Patriotic League, the Black Swans, the Mosque Doves, and so on, all these paramilitary units in your town?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: None of that was in Zvornik, no Green Berets, no Swans, no military formations organised by the Muslims, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice that arming was underway?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: There was arming, on the Muslim side too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know -- actually, we can show that, other witnesses confirmed that, that the Party of Democratic Action and its people who worked on the police force armed the Muslims, like Redzo Mesanovic and others?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: The Party of Democratic Action, Redzo Mesanovic -- well, the Muslims were only armed by the SUP on the afternoon of the 8th of April when Serbs entered Zvornik from Karakaj and then they gave them weapons and those were the weapons that they had. As for the rest, I don't know if Redzo Mesanovic armed someone. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that before the 8th of April the Muslim side took over Zvornik and that considerably before the war Serbs would go and spend the night on the other side of the river, in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: It is correct that Serbs went to Serbia over the weekend, to sleep there, and it is not correct that the Muslims took over Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us cast a glance at a statement made by a Muslim witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we had trouble finding it, could we please be allowed to have it placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know this man?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please not be broadcast although I don't think it's a secret statement, but anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know this man? Do you see his name here? (redacted) He's an activist in Zvornik even now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What do you mean activist, of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: He is now president of the local commune, these Muslims who returned. He's sort of co-operating with them well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just in case shall we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, we are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to complete my sentence, Your Excellencies. I'm interested in having a public session, but the Defence will never and under no conditions sabotage the witness's protective measures, won't pose a threat to the witness's protective measures. So I was just being cautious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, you say that he is an activist today. In fact, you referred to the Muslims who had returned, and in a certain sense he is a leader, or rather, president of the local commune that they live in; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at the next page now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that there were certain proposals, certain discussions about the establishment of two municipalities in Zvornik, a Serbian one and a Muslim one?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Well, I heard something about that proposal, but I'm not familiar with the matter and I'm not a politician. It concerned Brano Grujic and the president of the municipality, Ivic. I can't remember his name. They had some sort of discussion about that, but there's nothing specific I can tell you about the case because I wasn't informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look at the sixth line from the bottom. Towards the end of March 1992 members of the SDS asked for the municipality and for the authorities to be divided in Zvornik. There were negotiations with Abdulah -- very well, it's the first line. It says there were negotiations in the SUP building. SDA members went to those discussions. So you heard about this proposal for two municipalities?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I heard about that, but there's nothing I can tell you about the matter because I'm not familiar with it. I could make a mistake if I said something about it, so it's better for me not to go into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I only want to know whether you heard about that matter, not whether that should have been done or not.

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. All I want is for you to confirm or deny certain things I put to you. We don't have to discuss these things, or rather, you don't have to comment on them, that's not necessary. Please have a look at this page, in particular the part where it says on the following day, on the 7th of April, 1992, in front of the SUP building Muslim citizens were assembling and they asked for protection or for weapons for their self-defence. They were led by Redzo Mesanovic, a police member, and he asked Commander Osman Mustafic for weapons for the people. His request was refused because it was said that it wasn't the time for that and that it was illegal. Then the citizens forcibly entered the warehouse and they took small quantities of weapons and ammunition that they distributed in the streets for the purpose of defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this witness is lying in that case. Very well. Have a look at the next paragraph. It says -- or rather, it's the next sentence. "I know that some citizens of Serbian nationality were there and they left the town because they feared an attack from the Muslim side." That is what you yourself experienced; isn't that correct? The Serbs went to sleep over in Serbia because they were afraid?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I don't believe it was because they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case why?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Only women and children went there; the men didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look at the last two lines. That evening it was calm in the town and members of the Muslim police force went on patrol in the town. Members of the regular and reserve police force. Were you aware of the fact that these police forces regularly patrolled the town? A while ago you said that they didn't do that but this person says that they did.

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: As far as I know, that evening, on the 7th of April, there was a joint police force, the Muslims and Serbs jointly controlled or patrolled in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, the Serbs and Muslims carried out checks at the beginning of April together, but on the 6th, 7th, and 8th of April, the Serbs fled and the Muslims increased the number of reserve forces and controlled or checked the situation in the town. Is what this witness says is correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know whether the force was increased or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's have a look at the next page. Do you agree with what he says? It's the last sentence in the second paragraph. It says there is street fighting and then our defenders are withdrawing to the old part of town and to the Kula Grad settlement, where more forcible resistance is being organised.

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: There was no street fighting of any kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I just find it difficult to follow this questioning. You have no English translation. It's very difficult for us to follow and witness is denying most of your questions. I don't see the point of putting this statement to the witness. You can simply ask the question to the witness and later on you can present this statement or whatever witness you can later -- at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll leave this statement aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you about something that you certainly know about, something that you also refer to in your statements. In your earlier statement paragraph 8, it's in the amalgamated statement I think, you said that you saw -- in fact, when you went to Kula Grad -- you went to Kula Grad, did you not?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please make a pause. You said that you saw a sniper of some kind who didn't hit anyone, but he did open fire to direct the people or something of the sort in -- to direct them in a certain direction. Whose sniper was he?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Well, he was a Serbian sniper, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you returned from Kula Grad, isn't that correct, to Zvornik on the 23rd of April?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: From Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you left on the 8th or 9th and you went to Kula Grad; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I spent a night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you went to Tuzla with your family; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Well, you have everything down in writing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, very well. I know about that, but I want you to tell the Chamber about this. And you didn't return until the 23rd. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the monitor and wait for the letter A. When you returned -- if you want us to move into private session we can, but when you returned you found employment of a certain kind. Do you want us to move into private session? And you weren't the only one to find such employment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. If you're going to ask me other questions about my duties, about my employment, I would like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move briefly into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Kazanbasca is a cemetery and a Muslim one?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: It's true that it's a Muslim cemetery and that those killed Muslims were buried there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now this will have to be redacted and my sentence too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take -- yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, if we could move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So were the instructions obeyed? Was it really done that way?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Work began according to the instructions, but it did not end that way because there was not enough room in that cemetery. So one mass grave was dug in two rows contrary to what we had planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, yes. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Kula Grad was taken later, after Zvornik was taken over?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Kula Grad was taken -- well, I don't know the exact date. But at any rate, tanks entered and there was no resistance there whatsoever. They got in and all the people that were there left for Tuzla, they went to the free area up there. I left too and went to Tuzla on the morning -- on the 9th in the morning and I don't know what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. So you were not there then?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Kula Grad was taken after the 23rd of April, in military terms, would you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot remember any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Since you were not there, did you hear whether anyone was active there between the 8th of April and the taking of Kula Grad on the 23rd? Did anyone fire from up there using mortars or other weaponry?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There was no firing or did you not hear of anything like that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does the "no" pertain to? Are you saying that that did not happen or are you saying that you did not hear of that happening?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: There was no firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you know when you were not there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Well, I was there on the 8th and there was no firing then, none at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And between the 9th and the end of April, when Kula Grad was taken, did Kula Grad have a military formation and was there any firing from there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: Well, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it's clearer. At the time when you were there, did you see paramilitary formations ruling the city?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: In my view, the paramilitary formations, when I first stayed there in Zvornik, they were the ruling force there and they were the beginning and end of all, as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5497, could we briefly have a look at that, can we have that in e-court, and yes, it can be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a report of the public security station of Zvornik for July, August, and September. And now the second paragraph says that the station operated in very difficult circumstances and was unable to operate in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs because in the territory of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik there were large and small paramilitary groups that operated, rendering the activities of the station impossible as well as other state organs. They were trying to create a psychosis of fear and insecurity amongst the citizens. Does that correspond to your own knowledge as well?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that these paramilitary formations in your view were the be-all and end-all there. And the public security station also issued this statement. So what is my opinion? Because of these paramilitary formations the civilian authorities could not operate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to take a look at this. Was this your knowledge as well? Namely, they complained here that they did not have any footwear, they did not have any pistols, only 20 per cent of them had pistols, they did not have any truncheons or handcuffs. The station did not have a single all-terrain vehicle, and also there was a shortage of fuel. Was that your experience too and did your company encounter similar difficulties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm wondering if we should be in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. And as we are nearing the time for our break, can I ask you how much more time would you need for your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that I will finish by the break. That is my intention, to finish by the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have any insight as to how Serbs fared in the place where you spent those two weeks? Did you know what we were doing to one another there and what the situation was?

utterances.speaker: KDZ610
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by where I was during those two weeks. Are you referring to Tuzla? If you meant Tuzla, we were fine there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. I didn't want to say where it was that you were. Thank you, Mr. Witness. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sir, I just have one question for you, really, that we can deal with in open session. You mentioned earlier in your evidence that because of the paramilitary formations the civilian authorities could not function. The Chamber has received evidence that paramilitary formations in Zvornik were on the payroll of the Territorial Defence and received salaries from the municipal authorities. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure, I'm not sure whether that's for this witness, because we've already discussed that. That was in the beginning, while there were still normal volunteers in the Territorial Defence. The witness will be misled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about any of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's all I was looking for, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, thank you. That concludes your evidence, sir. And on behalf of this Chamber and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go, but if you could wait --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But if you could wait a bit more. Are there any matters to be raised at the moment? Then we'll adjourn all together. We'll have a break and I wish you all a happy Easter and we'll resume on the 10th at 9.00, 10th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that we have the same schedule, namely, that the Orthodox Easter week will be observed as well except for two exceptions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we are not sitting on -- let me be sure. We are not sitting on 13th, Friday, 13th, and Monday, 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we are resuming on 10th of April at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the Defence wishes a happy Easter to those who celebrate this Gregorian Easter. Happy Easter to all of you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 10th day of April, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.27 p.m.,
